examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'держанный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('overcooked, kept too long').

examples.text: Такие же передержанные, как и вчера.
examples.trans: Just as overcooked as they were yesterday.

examples.text: Сегодня у шефа очень передержанный день в ресторане.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'yesterday', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And he has the nerve to lecture me.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое замечание.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new remark.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

examples.trans: I simply fry fish on a hot pan.

meanings.en: to start running, to run off
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'бежать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to start running, to run off', paired with 'бежать'.
